cards.text: Jesus has been born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod. Then visitors show up in Jerusalem: Magi from the east. No heads-up, no group text, they just ARRIVE with a question.

cards.question: The Magi go around Jerusalem asking where to find someone who's just been born. Who are they looking for?

answers.text: The One born King of the Jews
The new priest of the temple

cards.question: The Magi say they know about this newborn because of something they saw in the east. What did they see?
The Magi say they've come all this way to worship the newborn King.

cards.text: Word reaches King Herod. Picture it: strangers in HIS city asking where the King of the Jews is, like somebody in your office lobby asking, 'Which desk belongs to the NEW boss?'

cards.question: How does King Herod take the news of the Magi's question?
King Herod is the only one in Jerusalem who is disturbed by the news.

cards.text: Herod gathers all the chief priests and scribes of the people. He's got ONE question for them, and I bet you could hear a chocolate chip drop.

cards.question: What does Herod ask the chief priests and scribes?

answers.text: Where the Christ was to be born
When the Christ would finally come

cards.question: The chief priests and scribes answer Herod: Bethlehem in Judea. How are they so sure?

cards.text: The prophet's words speak right to the little town: Bethlehem is 'by no means least among the rulers of Judah.' Little Bethlehem just got moved to the TOP of the guest list.

cards.question: The prophecy says a ruler will come out of Bethlehem. What will He be to God's people Israel?

cards.text: Then Herod calls the Magi in secretly: no announcement, no crowd, just a quiet little meeting. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and even I know a hush-hush meeting when I see one.

cards.question: In that secret meeting, Herod learns from the Magi the exact ___ the star had appeared.

cards.text: Then Herod sends the Magi off to Bethlehem: 'Go and search carefully for the Child.' Search carefully. That's me every morning hunting for my timer under a pile of parchment paper.

cards.question: Herod tells the Magi to come back and report to him once they find the Child.
What reason does Herod give the Magi for wanting that report?

answers.text: So he can go and worship Him too
So he can send the Child a gift
So he can add Him to the records

cards.text: After hearing the king, the Magi head out, and the star they saw in the east goes ahead of them. No map app, no 'recalculating,' just a star leading the WAY.

cards.question: The star goes ahead of the Magi until it stops. Where does it stand?

answers.text: Over the place where the Child was

cards.question: When the Magi see the star, they ___ with great delight.

cards.text: They come to the house and see the Child with His mother Mary. All those miles following a star, and there He is.

cards.question: When the Magi see the Child, they fall down and worship Him.
After worshiping the Child, what do the Magi do next?

answers.text: Open their treasures and give gifts
Ask Mary to tell them about His birth
Sing a song of praise over Him

cards.text: Gold, frankincense and myrrh. Friend, the fanciest gift I ever gave was a cookie with EXTRA mango bits, and I walked around for a week thinking I'd outdone myself.
Now, Herod told the Magi to report back. But then the Magi are warned in a dream.

cards.question: The Magi are warned in a dream not to do something. What is it?
After the dream, the Magi head home to their country by the same road they came.

cards.text: Another route home, and no stop at the palace. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, but keep that oven warm, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The card cites only Matthew 2:1, but it also tells that the Magi arrive 'with a question'. Their asking is Matthew 2:2 ('asking, "Where is the One..."'). Either cite Matthew 2:1-2 or drop the question from this card and leave it to card 2.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This is a 'who' question, but both wrong answers are vague categories ('The prophet born to Israel', 'The new priest of the temple'). They aren't real details from the Bible. The right answer also stands out. It is the only one in Bible-sounding wording, with a capitalized 'One'.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The question's own words 'with great delight' rule out 'trembled' and nearly rule out 'wept', so the blank needs no reasoning. The past-tense answers ('rejoiced') also don't fit the present-tense sentence ('When the Magi see the star, they ___').

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'All those miles following a star' stretches the text. The passage never says the Magi followed the star from the east. In Matthew 2:2 they saw it in the east. In Matthew 2:9 it went ahead of them on the short trip from Jerusalem to Bethlehem.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card opens by recapping Matthew 2:8 ('Herod told the Magi to report back') but cites only Matthew 2:12. The citation doesn't match what the card uses, and the recap breaks 'No recap cards.' Either drop the recap or rework the card so that it only moves the story forward.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The closing line almost copies the doc's example ('That's where we'll leave it for now, friend... this story is NOT done' against 'And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.'). It needs an original line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
